sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ngbandi language' and 'Spurious languages' (wikitext via API), citing Gueldemann, Tom. 2018. Historical linguistics and genealogical language classification in Africa. In Gueldemann (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of Africa, 58-444. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Nothing; states Kpatili is 'the name of a spurious Zande language for which there is no linguistic data' and that Gbayi/Kpatiri is a divergent Ngbandic language.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Kpatili [kym]' (the Internet Archive capture).
sources.note: Nothing; only population (4,500, 1996), location (south Mingala), 'Related to Nzakara [nzk]. Not intelligible with Gbayi [gyg], who are ethnically Kpatili', classification Ubangi > Zande > Zande-Nzakara.

sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond. 1988. Le kpatiri ou gbayi, une nouvelle langue du groupe ngbandi. In Yves Monino (ed.), Lexique comparatif des langues oubanguiennes, 35-49. Paris: Geuthner. (HAL author version hal-00344525.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (0 hits for accent/intensite/stress/prosod). Describes Gbayi (gbay1278), the language actually spoken by the Kpatiri: CV(CV) canonical shapes, 7 vowels, and tone -- three level tones B/M/H, verbal tone classes B, M, HB (sec. 11), nominal schemes B, M, H, HM, HB, BM, BH, MB, MH (sec. 13), grammatical H tone in conjugation (sec. 12), optional phrase-final falling contour on nouns (sec. 14).

sources.note: Nothing; states that only a Ngbandic language (Gbayi) is attested for the Kpatili and the Zande-Nzakara 'Kpatili' [kym] is pure speculation.
